newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Cavallo indicted by judge - agencies.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo indicted by judge - agencies.

text.p: An Argentine judge said he indicted former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo on Monday "for having business interests that were incompatible with public office," two news agencies reported.

The indictment came on the back of evidence showing that Cavallo had tried to prevent private sector postal firm OCASA from winning a tender to carry out mail services for the state mortgage-bank, Banco Hipotecario Nacional, Judge Norberto Oyarbide said, according to the state-owned Telam and independent DyN news agencies.
Guillermo Francos, Cavallo's lawyer, said he will appeal the indictment and accused Judge Norberto Oyarbide of being motivated by "political interests," the agencies said.
Francos was not immediately available for comment.

The case dates back to April 1996 when Alejandro Barassi, the head of OCASA, first accused Cavallo, the then economy minister, of interfering in the tender for the postal services at Banco Hipotecario Nacional.

OCASA is owned by Alfredo Yabran, a businessman Cavallo has long accused of heading what he terms as a crime syndicate. Yabran has denied the charges and filed a defamation suit against the former economy minister.

Since being fired last July by President Carlos Menem, Cavallo has staged a single-handed campaign against corruption, accusing several ministers, judges and businessmen of corruption. Many of them are suing him.
Cavallo launched his bid for a congressional seat in October mid-term elections last week and admitted his sights are on the 1999 or 2003 presidential elections.

Judge Oyarbide, cited by the news agencies, said Cavallo's efforts were carried out "to benefit a company (postal firm Encotesa), which although state-owned, was headed by a person who, as is widespread public knowledge, is closely linked to Cavallo."

Roque Maccarone, the former secretary of finance, banks and insurance, was indicted with Cavallo for "having recommended Cavallo to proceed with what he is now accused of," said Oyarbide, the agencies reported.

The former minister's accusations of Yabran was part of the reason for Yabran recently being summoned by a congressional committee to a full day of grilling on his relations with private security firms.
